title: Fizlet 0.19 is out
subtitle: A game engine for the page, measured to the byte.
lead: Fizlet is a micro game and animation engine for the DOM, by Chris Cooley. Version 0.19.0 is the one we launch with: a 3,439-byte kernel (gzip, budget 4 KB), 20 bricks that each have their own budget, and nine rules every one of them is tested against. It is MIT, with no runtime dependencies.

items.label: the kernel, minified and gzipped (budget 4,096 B, checked in CI)
a page build: kernel, `fizlet/slot`, `fizlet/input` and `fizlet/fx` (budget 7,168 B)
young-generation GCs in one million kernel steps of a busy system, on Node 24
frames a second a capped hero asks for (`fps: 30`), down from one per vsync

body.text: Fizlet plays on the page you already have. Every engine on a page shares one `requestAnimationFrame` and steps at a fixed 60 Hz. Pools and the event ring have a fixed size and refuse work when full. Every change to the page goes through one ledger, so `destroy()` gives the page back exactly. We call that Recall.

It is built for two jobs. One is small games that run inside a page and use its letters and buttons as the board. The other is page heroes and interactive diagrams that should cost nothing while they are still. Both are the same kernel with different bricks.

items.title: The kernel
items.body: `createEngine`: the shared clock, the fixed step with a catch-up cap, auto-pause, bounded pools, the event ring, a seeded random and the ledger. 3,439 B gzip.

items.title: Game bricks
items.body: Input and a touch pad, a spatial hash, a board with A* paths, pooled effects, pixel sprites, a synth, a HUD, match flow, waves, drops and score, steering, a coach and the arcade shell. Each is its own import.

items.title: Page bricks
items.body: `fizlet/slot` fills an Astro animation slot with a lazy scene, `fizlet/camera` pans and zooms a DOM stage, and `fizlet/timeline`, new in 0.19.0, runs keyframes on the kernel clock (2,050 B gzip).

items.title: Multiplayer
items.body: `fizlet/presence` exchanges inputs in lockstep, 12 bytes a message (1,792 B gzip), and `syncCheck` finds the first frame two peers disagree on. The room server is a Cloudflare Worker in the repo.

items: **npm.** `npm install fizlet` is not published yet. The site hosts the same builds: `fizlet.js` (one script tag, every brick but debug, 13,312 B gzip) and the ES modules under `/dist/`.
**The API is 0.x.** Minor versions can still break an API; when one does, the release notes say so under **Breaking**, as 0.10.0 did for `fizlet/sprite` and `fizlet/camera`.
**Rooms.** The room server's gate is a demo gate: invite codes, not accounts. A seat that leaves mid-game makes the others wait.
**Ports.** Five games run on the kernel. Swarm Protocol, the last, is in review.

body.text: Fizlet runs five of the games on the DOM VIRUS arcade, from Battlefield Blitz to Null Invaders, and every hero and gallery animation on this site. The games live at [domvirus.com](https://domvirus.com/); this site is about the engine under them.

items.a: No. It is an engine: a kernel and bricks you import one at a time, with no runtime dependencies. It owns nothing on your page it can't give back.

items.q: How do I try it in a minute?
items.a: Add `<script src="https://fizlet.com/fizlet.js"></script>` and run the ten-line quick start: click the canvas for the blast.
Every version has release notes on the site, generated from the changelog, with the sizes measured when it shipped.
